name: POWER
description: POWER raises a number to the power of another number.
tldr: POWER calculates number^power, raising a base number to an exponent.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The base number to raise to a power.

parameters.name: power
parameters.description: The exponent to raise the base to.

basicExample.explanation: Returns 2 raised to the power of 3, which equals 8.

advancedExamples.title: Calculate compound interest
advancedExamples.description: Compute future value with compound interest
advancedExamples.explanation: Calculates future value using the formula PV*(1+r)^n.

advancedExamples.title: Calculate nth root
advancedExamples.description: Find the cube root of a number
advancedExamples.explanation: Raises 27 to the 1/3 power to get the cube root.

howItWorks: POWER computes number^power by multiplying the base number by itself power times.

howToSteps.name: Select output cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where the result should appear.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the calculated power.

limitations: Negative numbers raised to non-integer powers return #NUM!.
For roots, use fractional exponents like 1/2 for square root.

commonErrors.cause: Negative number raised to non-integer power
commonErrors.fix: Use ABS for negative bases or use integer exponents.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: POWER works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Is POWER the same as the ^ operator?
Can I use decimal exponents?
faq.answer: Yes, POWER(10, 0.5) calculates the square root of 10.
